findings.text: the run's live record still declares the original mutation over dispatch.py ('remove the own-run exclusion from the out-of-repository conflict path in a scratch copy of dispatch.py; the own-claim case must report scope-conflict') while the red log this manifest names opens with the re-scoped mutation over reckon/cli.py, so the declaration is not a substring of the log; I ran the declaration check exactly as promotion calls it and it raised CrewError (logs/review-promotion-refusal.log), so promoting this run on gate=passed needs the declaration corrected to the mutation the log shows, or --waive-negative-control carrying the re-scope as the reason.

two files outside the declared write paths carry the change — reckon/cli.py (the payload) and tests/test_crew.py (its exact-mapping assertion) — and they were forced: the re-scope required a distinct field for the claimant (resume-1-advice.txt:6-9) while keeping the write paths unchanged (:13), and the refusal dict is assembled only at reckon/cli.py:1561, so no dispatch.py-only change can add the key its test asserts; the worker disclosed both edits and left the check_manifest finding standing, so the only unmet condition was that the peer channel had no wired coordinator to grant an extension.

the head gate log's first line is pytest's progress row, so the log names no revision, tree or command, and scope-delta.log:1 and base-gate.log:1 are the same; base-arm.log carries module= and cwd= but no revision=, and that module= names the reviewing worktree in error, so the 9 passed is attributable to the reviewed head only through the manifest's prose — though the reviewed worktree is clean and byte-identical to 119253f5 for both changed paths, and my re-run in that worktree reproduced 9 passed with revision, tree, command and imported module captured mechanically.

the delivered base arm's tracebacks sit at tests/test_scope_refusal_names_its_claimant.py:246 and :267 while the committed file's two run_id assertions sit at :244 and :265, so the delivered log is a run of an earlier revision of the test file and is not reproducible byte-for-byte from the commit; against the committed file the same two assertion failures reproduce at :244 and :265 with the third, positive-control test passing (logs/review-base-arm-rerun2.log), so the content claim holds.

the two suite arms are recorded as prose under baseline_suite and after_suite, which the review read path resolves to a nonexistent relative path, so a read-time annotation reports the added-failure count unmeasured; the pair the prose names measures the run at zero added failures by id, derived here with the module's own added_failures_from_gate_logs and stored with added_failures_source, and a JSON suite observation would have made it machine-readable.
